---
title: "Week 1: Data as Social Construct"
---

## Theme: The Social Construction of Public Health Evidence

Every dataset reflects choices about what to count, who counts, and who
decides. This week we examine how framing shapes public health evidence
and how administrative law and agency power turn \'data\' into
\'crisis.\' We introduce R Markdown for reproducible reporting and
explore publicly available health data resources. We also examine the
Google Flu Trends episode as a cautionary tale about how big data can
mislead as well as illuminate. Note: Monday January 18 is Martin Luther
King Jr. Day --- no classes. Week 2 begins Tuesday January 19.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Administrative law and the power of health agencies
(CDC, FDA) to define \'crisis\' through mandatory data reporting
standards; the Paperwork Reduction Act and federal data collection
authority.

**Health Focus:** How surveillance data shapes resource allocation and
public health response; limitations of administrative data in capturing
structural drivers of health.

**Data:** CDC BRFSS (Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System,
cdc.gov/brfss); CDC NHIS (National Health Interview Survey,
cdc.gov/nchs/nhis); CDC ILINet influenza surveillance data
(gis.cdc.gov/grasp/fluview).

**R Code:** R Markdown setup and YAML headers; loading CSV data with
readr; exploring codebooks; computing frequency tables with dplyr
(group_by, summarise, count); basic ggplot2 bar charts; knitting to
HTML.

- Initialize GitHub repository; create a new .Rmd file with YAML header
  (title, author, date, output: html_document)

- Load the provided BRFSS subset from Carmen using read_csv(); examine
  variable names and class with glimpse() and head()

- Compute the prevalence of 3 health outcomes by state using group_by()
  and summarise(); display as a sorted bar chart in ggplot2

- Load CDC ILINet weekly flu surveillance CSV (provided on Carmen); plot
  a time series of influenza-like illness (ILI) rates by week using
  ggplot2 geom_line(); compare pre- and post-2009 pandemic patterns

- Knit the completed document to HTML; review the output and discuss:
  what does the ILINet data measure, and what does it miss?
